children: Law firm Linklaters said on Thursday that it has hired longtime partner Mark Gordon from Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, marking the latest departure from the New York firm amid a hot market for senior U.S. legal talent.
Gordon will join Linklaters in November as managing partner of its Americas division and co-chair of global mergers and acquisitions, the London-founded firm said.

His recent deals have included representing artificial decking maker AZEK in its $8.75 billion acquisition by fiber-cement maker James Hardie Industries last year, and drugmaker Alexion Pharmaceuticals in its $39 billion sale to AstraZeneca in 2021.

Wachtell lost a high-profile litigation team in July, with William Savitt, who co-chaired the firm's executive ‌committee and litigation department, moving with five other partners to Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher. Sidley Austin said earlier this month that it brought on former Wachtell partner Deborah Paul to co-lead its tax practice.

Restructuring partner Joshua Feltman left Wachtell for Kirkland & Ellis in April. Kirkland offered Feltman a pay package of $80 million over three years, according to the Financial Times, which cited people familiar with the matter.
Wachtell spokespeople did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Gordon's exit and other recent departures.
Linklaters is among a group of top UK-founded firms that have sought to grow their U.S. market share through aggressive hiring.
“We have a clear ambition: to build a top-tier team in the U.S. as a core part of our global offering," Linklaters senior partner and chair Aedamar Comiskey said in a statement.
Gordon was not immediately available for comment. He takes over the Americas leadership position from Tom McGrath, whose term ended, Linklaters said.

He will work on the firm's U.S. growth alongside dealmaker George Casey, chair of the Americas and global chair of corporate, who joined Linklaters from Shearman & Sterling in 2024. The firm has doubled its revenue and quadrupled ​profits over the past four years in the United States.
Linklaters' other recent U.S. hires have included a litigation and sports team from Paul Weiss and Johnson & Johnson's global litigation leader, Erik Haas.
